evidence.result: 10 s synthetic mix (kick/snare, bass, say voice) at 44.1 kHz stereo: 4 stems, 441000 samples each. Correlation margins drums 0.835, bass 0.961, vocals 0.996. SDR drums 8.0, bass 11.1, vocals 16.1 dB. Sum residual SNR 20.1 dB. Stems byte-identical across two runs. htdemucs, CPU, torch 2.15.0, numpy 2.5.5.

install.macos: uv venv --python 3.12 <venv>; uv pip install -r examples/demucs-stem-separation/requirements.txt (torch CPU index, demucs 4.1.0, numpy pinned: demucs does not declare numpy on arm64)

summary: Research code and command-line interface for separating recorded music into stems using neural models. The original repository is archived and no longer maintained; model and weight terms require separate checks.
use_when: Research offline music-stem separation on suitable licensed audio
Evaluate separation quality before using stems in a production
avoid_when: Need maintained or safety-supported software without a prior evaluation
Need simple audio trimming or muxing: FFmpeg
license: MIT (source code). Model weights: upstream README says licence not clear, likely CC-BY-NC (checked 2026-11-24); input and output rights not assessed
